title: Abstraction in Art and Programming
description: This curriculum introduces learners to abstraction by connecting abstract visual art with code.

competencies.name: Observe visual structure
competencies.description: Identify simplified forms, contrast, balance, and compositional relationships in abstract art.
competencies.longDescription: Learners inspect abstract artworks and identify what has been simplified, what has been emphasized, and how shape, contrast, color, and balance create visual structure.

competencies.name: Connect abstraction in art and code
competencies.description: Explain how abstraction appears in both visual art and programming.
competencies.longDescription: Learners compare how artists simplify and organize forms with how programmers name, compose, and reuse code structures to express essential ideas.

competencies.name: Compose graphics
competencies.description: Combine simple graphical elements into a larger image.
competencies.longDescription: Learners build complete images from smaller graphics, mirroring how abstract artworks can be reconstructed from a few essential parts.

competencies.name: Primitive graphics
competencies.description: Create images from basic geometric shapes.
competencies.longDescription: Learners use primitive PyTamaro graphics such as rectangles and circles as the raw building blocks for larger compositions.

competencies.name: Call functions
competencies.description: Use function calls to produce values and graphics.
competencies.longDescription: Learners read and write function calls to build graphics from named operations and reusable pieces.

competencies.name: Use colors
competencies.description: Apply color purposefully in a graphic composition.
competencies.longDescription: Learners use color to create contrast, hierarchy, and mood while keeping focus on the essential structure of an abstract image.

competencies.name: Decompose visual patterns
competencies.description: Break an image into smaller reusable visual parts.
competencies.longDescription: Learners identify the key parts of an artwork and describe how those parts can be rebuilt in code as separate graphical pieces or helper functions.

competencies.name: Define functions
competencies.description: Define a function that packages a reusable idea.
competencies.longDescription: Learners define functions that hide construction details behind a meaningful name, making code easier to understand and reuse.

competencies.name: Use names
competencies.description: Store important values in descriptive names.
competencies.longDescription: Learners bind important values, colors, graphics, and intermediate results to names that communicate their role in a program.

competencies.name: Parameterize drawings
competencies.description: Use parameters to control size, position, or proportion in code.
competencies.longDescription: Learners create functions with parameters so that a drawing can vary while preserving its internal relationships.

competencies.name: Arithmetic operators
competencies.longDescription: Learners use arithmetic operations to compute dimensions and relationships instead of hard-coding every value.

competencies.name: Compose expressions
competencies.description: Build larger computations from smaller expressions.
competencies.longDescription: Learners nest and combine expressions to describe more complex visual relationships in compact code.

competencies.name: Use repetition in code
competencies.description: Recognize and implement repeated visual structures through code.
competencies.longDescription: Learners connect repeated forms in artwork with repeated structures in programming, such as loops, generated sequences, or systematic combinations.

competencies.name: Literal sequences
competencies.description: Write specific sequences of values directly in code.
competencies.longDescription: Learners create lists or other sequences by explicitly writing the desired values in source code.

competencies.name: Generate sequences
competencies.longDescription: Learners generate collections of values through code rather than listing each value manually.

competencies.name: Rotate graphics
competencies.description: Rotate graphics to create new arrangements and symmetries.
competencies.longDescription: Learners transform graphics by rotating them, connecting geometric transformations in code with compositional choices in abstract art.

competencies.name: Controlled variation
competencies.description: Use randomization with structure behind it.
competencies.longDescription: Learners form algorithms that include random components while still following clear rules and constraints.
